spans.s:
śrotriya
(‘one who is well-versed in the Śruti [Vedas]’)
------------------------------------------
Vedas are known as Śruti. Hence a श्रोत्रिय is one who is well-versed in the Śrutis.
However, the word has often been used in a technical sense. According to the Padmapurāṇa (Uttarakhaṇḍa, Chapter 116) one who is born to ब्राह्मण parents is called a ब्राह्मण. By undergoing the सṁस्कारस् or sacraments, he becomes a द्विज (‘twice born’). By studying the वेदस् he becomes a विप्र. If he is endowed with all the three factors, he becomes a श्रोत्रिय.
According to another version (as given in some of the धर्मशास्त्रस्) a श्रोत्रिय is one who has studied his branch of the Veda, along with the six वेदाङ्गस् and is performing the six allotted duties, viz., अध्ययन (study of the वेदस्), adhyāpana (teaching the वेदस्), yajana (performing sacrifices), yājana (getting the sacrifices done by others), दान (giving gifts) and pratigraha (receiving gifts).
In śrāddha ceremonies, feeding a श्रोत्रिय is considered highly meritorious.
A king should see that no श्रोत्रिय in his kingdom remains uncared for.
